definition_zh: 忠告；劝告；律师
definition_en: advice given to someone, to give such advice, or a lawyer who speaks for a person in court
core_image: 一位长辈把两条路的利弊摊在桌上，让年轻人自己选
scene: 年轻人想退学，老师没有替他决定，只把利弊一条条摆出来。 She counselled him to wait one more term.
sceneCN: 这里 counsel 指「劝告」（第 2 个义项：给出建议而不替人决定）；句意是她劝他再等一个学期。

pos.zh: 忠告；建议；律师；法律顾问

derivatives.zh: 顾问；辅导员
心理咨询；辅导
顾问（美式拼写）

senses.title: Advice from someone wise
senses.definition: careful advice given to someone about what they should do
senses.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做而给出的慎重建议
senses.example: He sought counsel from his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他向年迈的老师寻求忠告。
senses.why: A second pair of eyes can see the road you cannot.
senses.whyCN: 多一双眼睛，就能看见你看不见的那条路。

senses.title: To advise someone
senses.definition: to give someone advice about a decision or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 就决定或行动方案向某人提出建议
senses.example: She counselled him to wait one more term.
senses.exampleCN: 她劝他再等一个学期。
senses.why: Advice is a lamp handed over, not a hand that pushes.
senses.whyCN: 劝告是递过去的一盏灯，而不是推人的一只手。

senses.title: A lawyer in court
senses.definition: a lawyer who represents someone in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中代表某人的律师
senses.example: The defence counsel asked for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师请求多给一些时间。
senses.why: In court, advice must stand up and speak aloud.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，建议必须站起来大声说话。

intro.en: Counsel comes from Latin consilium, advice or plan, from consulere, to consult or take counsel.
intro.cn: counsel 来自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），源自动词 consulere（商议、征询）。

items.en: Consulere meant to consult or ask for advice.
items.cn: consulere 意为商议或征询建议。

items.en: Consilium named a plan or a piece of advice.
items.cn: consilium 指计划或一条建议。

items.en: Conseil kept both the advice and the act of advising.
items.cn: conseil 既指建议，也指提建议这件事。

items.en: English counsel meant advice and the giving of it.
items.cn: 英语 counsel 指建议以及给出建议。

items.en: It also names the lawyer who gives advice in court.
items.cn: 它也表示在法庭上提供建议的律师。

note.en: The look-alike group sets council, consul and console beside counsel, and the meaning group names advice and lawyers.
note.cn: 形近组把 council、consul 与 console 放在 counsel 旁边，近义组列出建议与律师的说法。

entries.definition: a group chosen to make decisions
an official who helps citizens abroad
entries.definitionCN: 在海外帮助本国公民的官员

entries.definition: to comfort a sad person
an opinion about what someone should do
entries.definitionCN: 关于某人该怎么做的一种意见

entries.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
entries.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他该怎么做

entries.definition: a person trained to argue legal cases
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、办理法律案件的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a lamp passed to a young hand, then move to a gentle warning and to a lawyer standing up in court.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从递到年轻人手里的灯开始，再到一句温和的劝阻，最后到法庭上站起来的律师。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.
normal.cn: council 是团体，counsel 是它给出的建议。

normal.en: The single l points like a lamp toward one path.
normal.cn: 中间的一个 l 像一盏灯，指向一条路。

normal.en: To counsel is to hand over a map and step back.
normal.cn: 劝告就是递过一张地图，然后退后一步。

normal.en: A defence counsel stands between a person and a sentence.
normal.cn: 辩护律师站在一个人与一份判决之间。

normal.en: Keep your own counsel means keep the map in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep your own counsel 就是把地图留在自己口袋里。

abstract.en: Picture two roads drawn on a napkin.
abstract.cn: 想象餐巾纸上画出的两条路。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a lamp but not pulling an arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举着灯，却不拉扯别人的手臂。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet voice in a room full of loud choices.
abstract.cn: 想象满是喧闹选择的屋子里，一个安静的声音。

examples.en: She counselled him to wait one more term.
examples.cn: 她劝他再等一个学期。

examples.en: He sought counsel from his old teacher.
examples.cn: 他向年迈的老师寻求忠告。

examples.en: The defence counsel asked for more time.
examples.cn: 辩护律师请求多给一些时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 counsel 记成「靠 sell」：好建议不是拿来卖的，而是靠得住的人私下给的忠告。

root: 源自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），来自 consulere（商议、征询），本指商议后给出的意见，后也指提供意见的律师。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan offered to a friend, to the act of offering it, and at last to the lawyer who offers it in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 从给朋友的一个方案，到给出方案这一动作，最后到在法庭上给出意见的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths laid on a table, with a lamp beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开两条路，旁边放着一盏灯。

branches.en: A trusted voice names the safer path.
branches.cn: 一个可信的声音指出更稳的那条路。

branches.en: The act of advising leaves the choice where it belongs.
branches.cn: 劝告这一动作，把选择留在该在的人手里。

branches.en: In court the advice becomes a public argument.
branches.cn: 在法庭上，建议变成公开的辩论。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name one act from two sides.
branches.cn: 名词与动词从两侧说同一个动作。

branches.en: A lawyer also counsels a client, but with the law at hand.
branches.cn: 律师也在劝告当事人，只是手里多了一部法律。

intro.en: Counsel is a base word from Latin consilium, with English endings for the person and the activity.
intro.cn: counsel 是源自拉丁语 consilium 的词根词，再由英语词尾派生出人物与活动。

latinIntro.en: The consulting base consul- also appears in consult, consultation and consul.
latinIntro.cn: 表示商议的词基 consul- 也出现在 consult、consultation 与 consul 中。

definition_zh: 理性的；合理的；有理数的；心智健全的
definition_en: based on reason rather than feeling; sensible and logical; expressible as a ratio of two integers; able to think clearly
core_image: 案头一列摆得整整齐齐、编号清楚的卡片
scene: 会议桌旁，人人按次序发言，论点一条条摆得明白。 She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
sceneCN: 这里 rational 是「合理的」（第 2 个义项：合乎道理与逻辑）；句意为她为延误给出了合理的解释。画面里可留意：按次序的发言、条理清楚的论点。

pos.zh: 理性的；合理的；有理数的；心智健全的

derivatives.zh: rational 加 -ly，指理性地、合理地
rational 加 -ity，指理性、合理性
rational 加 -e，指理由说明
ir- 与 rational 复合，指非理性的

senses.title: Guided by reason
senses.definition: based on reason rather than on feeling or impulse
senses.definitionCN: 基于道理而非情感或冲动
senses.example: A rational person checks the facts before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 理性的人会先核对事实再作决定。
senses.why: Rational comes from Latin ratio, reason itself, so the adjective first describes a mind that works by reckoning.
senses.whyCN: rational 来自拉丁语 ratio，即理性本身，因此这个形容词首先描述按计算运作的心智。

senses.title: Sensible and logical
senses.definition: sensible, logical and free of contradiction, used of explanations, plans and choices
senses.definitionCN: 合乎道理、有逻辑且不自相矛盾，用于解释、计划与选择
senses.example: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。
senses.why: If a mind works by reason, then what such a mind produces is also called rational: a sound, well-grounded account.
senses.whyCN: 如果心智按理性运作，那么这种心智产出的东西也被称为 rational：一个站得住脚、有根据的说法。

senses.title: Expressible as a ratio
senses.definition: of a number, able to be written as the ratio of two whole numbers
senses.definitionCN: 指一个数可以写成两个整数之比
senses.example: One half is a rational number.
senses.exampleCN: 二分之一是一个有理数。
senses.why: Mathematics took the word literally: a rational number is one that can be expressed as a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 数学把这个词按字面使用：有理数就是可以表示成比率的数。

senses.title: Able to think clearly
senses.definition: able to think and judge clearly, not confused or insane
senses.definitionCN: 能够清楚思考和判断，未混乱或失常
senses.example: The patient remained rational throughout the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人整夜都保持清醒理智。
senses.why: Reason is the mark of a sound mind, so rational came to describe a person whose thinking is intact.
senses.whyCN: 理性是健全心智的标志，因此 rational 也用来形容思维完好的人。

intro.en: Rational comes from Latin rationalis, belonging to ratio, reason or reckoning; English borrowed it to describe what follows reason.
intro.cn: rational 来自拉丁语 rationalis，意为属于 ratio（理性、计算）的；英语借它来描述合乎理性的事物。

items.en: Ratio meant reckoning and reason, the power by which amounts and arguments are worked out.
items.cn: ratio 意为计算与理性，是推算数量与论证的力量。

items.en: Rationalis meant belonging to reason, and it described a thinking being and a well-grounded argument alike.
items.cn: rationalis 意为属于理性的，既形容会思考的存在，也形容有根据的论证。

items.en: English took rationalis as rational, keeping the link between reason and sound judgment.
items.cn: 英语把 rationalis 借作 rational，保留理性与健全判断之间的联系。

items.en: Mathematicians used rational for numbers that can be written as a ratio of integers.
items.cn: 数学家把 rational 用于可写成整数之比的数。

items.en: Modern English uses rational for reasoned thought, sensible plans, such numbers, and a sound mind.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rational 指有理性的思维、合理的计划、这类数，以及健全的心智。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the root word and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is reasonable and sane.
note.cn: 形近组收词根词与近形词；近义组收表示合理与清醒的词。

entries.definition: The relation between two amounts.
A set of reasons for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事给出的一套理由。

entries.definition: A fixed share of supplies.
Not guided by reason.
Following clear rules of reasoning.
Showing good judgment.
Fair and based on good sense.
Of a sound mind.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as belonging to reason, then passes to sound arguments, to numbers written as ratios, and to a mind that is intact.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「属于理性」开始，转到有根据的论证，再到可写成比率的数，最后到完好的心智。

normal.en: Rational comes from ratio, reason, so a rational act is one that reason can account for.
normal.cn: rational 来自 ratio（理性），因此理性的行为是理性能够解释的行为。

normal.en: A rational explanation is one that holds together without contradiction.
normal.cn: 合理的解释是前后一致、不自相矛盾的解释。

normal.en: A rational number is simply a number that can be written as a ratio.
normal.cn: 有理数就是可以写成一个比的数。

normal.en: Rational and rationale are close, but rationale is the set of reasons behind a choice.
normal.cn: rational 与 rationale 相近，但 rationale 是一项选择背后的那套理由。

normal.en: Irrational is the direct opposite, built with the negative prefix ir-.
normal.cn: irrational 是直接的反义词，由否定前缀 ir- 构成。

abstract.en: To be rational is to let reasons, not moods, decide.
abstract.cn: 理性，就是让理由而非情绪作决定。

abstract.en: A rational plan can be explained to anyone who asks why.
abstract.cn: 合理的计划能向任何追问原因的人解释清楚。

abstract.en: What is rational is not always what is kind.
abstract.cn: 合乎理性的，并不总是仁慈的。

examples.en: A rational person checks the facts before deciding.
examples.cn: 理性的人会先核对事实再作决定。

examples.en: She gave a rational explanation for the delay.
examples.cn: 她为延误给出了合理的解释。

examples.en: One half is a rational number.
examples.cn: 二分之一是一个有理数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉申诺」——凡事列出理由、算清条理，记住 rational 是理性的、合理的。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、理性）→ rationalis（属于理性的）→ 英语 rational；同族有 rationally、rationality、rationale、irrational。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reason; the senses divide into a reasoned mind, a sound argument, a number written as a ratio, and a mind that is intact.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「理性」；义项分为有理性的心智、有根据的论证、可写成比率的数，以及健全的心智。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of cards laid out in clear numbered order, each argument in its place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按清晰编号摆开的卡片，每条论证都各在其位。

branches.en: a person checking facts before speaking
branches.cn: 开口前先核对事实的人

branches.en: an argument that holds together
branches.cn: 前后一致、站得住脚的论证

branches.en: one half written as a ratio
branches.cn: 写成一个比的二分之一

branches.en: a patient thinking clearly through the night
branches.cn: 整夜思维清醒的病人

branches.en: a reason-driven mind and the sound argument it produces
branches.cn: 受理智驱动的心智与它产出的可靠论证

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with Latin and English suffixes and one negative prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由拉丁语与英语后缀，以及一个否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratio, reason, and rationalis, belonging to reason, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratio（理性）与 rationalis（属于理性的）是有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a number writable as a ratio

definition_zh: 更新；使现代化；向……提供最新消息；更新；最新消息
definition_en: to make something more modern or bring it up to date, or a report with the newest facts
core_image: 一册日历被逐页翻到最新一天，旧的一页被撕下，新的数字露出来
scene: 手机在夜里弹出提示，说系统需要重启才能装上新版本。 The app asks you to update it before the new features can be used.
sceneCN: 这里 update 是「更新」（第 1 个义项：使内容变为最新的）；句意为这个应用要求你先更新，之后才能使用新功能。日历被翻到最新那一页，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 更新；最新消息；最新版本

collocations.zh: 向某人通报……的最新情况

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「已更新的；最新的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「更新过程」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「更新程序；更新者」
由本词的两个部件加连字符构成，义为「最新的」

senses.title: Make it current
senses.definition: to change something so that it contains the newest information or works in the newest way
senses.definitionCN: 改动某物，使其包含最新的信息或以最新的方式工作
senses.example: She updates the price list every Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周一早上更新价目表。
senses.why: Up brings the thing to the present, and date names that present: the record is lifted to today.
senses.whyCN: up 把东西提到当下，date 指这个当下：记录被抬到了今天。

senses.title: Tell someone the news
senses.definition: to give someone the latest facts about a situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某一情况的最新事实告诉某人
senses.example: The officer updated the family on the search every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 警官每天晚上向这家人通报搜寻的进展。
senses.why: The same lifting happens in words instead of records: the listener is brought up to the current state of affairs.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「抬高」发生在消息而非记录上：听者被带到事情的当前状态。

senses.title: A newer version
senses.definition: a new version of a program, file, or document that replaces the old one
senses.definitionCN: 取代旧版本的程序、文件或文档的新版本
senses.example: The update fixed a fault that closed the program without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次更新修复了一个会让程序毫无预兆关闭的故障。
senses.why: The verb turns into a countable noun, so each act of bringing something current becomes a thing you can install.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为可数名词，于是每一次「带到当下」都成了可以安装的东西。

senses.title: A short news report
senses.definition: a short piece of news giving the newest facts about a running story
senses.definitionCN: 关于进行中的事件的最新事实的简短报道
senses.example: We will bring you an update at nine o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 我们将在九点为您带来最新报道。
senses.why: News is a story that keeps moving, so it needs the same word: a short report that catches the audience up.
senses.whyCN: 新闻是不断变动的事件，因此需要同一个词：一则把听众带到最新进展的短报道。

senses.title: Bring something up to standard
senses.definition: to modernize a building, system, or machine so that it meets present needs
senses.definitionCN: 对建筑、系统或机器进行现代化改造，使其满足当下需要
senses.example: The library was updated with new lights and faster computers.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆翻新了照明，换上了更快的电脑。
senses.why: Here the standard being reached is not a date but the present day itself: an old building is brought up to how people live now.
senses.whyCN: 这里要达到的标准不是某个日期，而是当下本身：旧建筑被提到人们今天生活的方式。

intro.en: Update is a modern compound: the English adverb up joined to the French-derived verb date.
intro.cn: update 是近代复合词：英语副词 up 加源自法语的动词 date。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and the Latin phrase data, items given, became the source of date in the sense of a written day.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dare 意为「给予」，短语 data（给予之物）成为 date 指「日期」的来源。

items.en: French date named the day on which a document is given or made.
items.cn: 古法语 date 指文件签发或写成的日期。

items.en: English took date for the day of writing, and later used the verb date for marking a time.
items.cn: 英语以 date 指写作日期，后来动词 date 表示标注时间。

items.en: Up and date were combined in the twentieth century, first for keeping records current.
items.cn: 二十世纪把 up 与 date 合成，最初用于使记录保持最新。

items.en: Computers made update a household word, as patches and news feeds both began to update themselves.
items.cn: 计算机让 update 家喻户晓，补丁与新闻推送都开始自我更新。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with up and date; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of renewal and news with different scopes.
note.cn: 形近组收由 up 与 date 构成的词；近义组收表示更新与通报的动词，范围不同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning current, keeping the newest facts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最新的」，保持最新信息。

entries.definition: No longer current, old enough to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过时的」，旧到该被替换。

entries.definition: A day of the month, or a meeting with someone romantically.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「日期」，也可指约会。

entries.definition: Adjective for something already made current.
To send data to a server; it shares the prefix, not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上传」，只共享前缀。

entries.definition: To raise something to a higher grade or better model.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「升级」，把某物提到更高等级或更好的型号。

entries.definition: To make valid again, or to begin again after a break.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「续期、更新」，使重新有效或重新开始。

entries.definition: To bring an old building or system up to present standards.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「现代化」，把旧建筑或系统提到当下标准。

entries.definition: To change a text or a plan after looking at it again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修订」，重看后加以改动。

entries.definition: To make something feel or look new again, or to reload a screen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恢复、刷新」，包括刷新屏幕。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the up plus date structure and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 up 加 date 的结构，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Up means to a higher level and date means the day: bring it up to today.
normal.cn: up 表示「向上」，date 表示「日期」：把它提到今天。

normal.en: A software update replaces the old version quietly at night.
normal.cn: 软件更新在夜里悄悄替换旧版本。

normal.en: Update someone on a matter means telling them the latest facts.
normal.cn: 向某人通报某事的最新情况，用的就是 update。

normal.en: Up-to-date is the adjective, outdated is the opposite.
normal.cn: up-to-date 是形容词，outdated 是它的反面。

normal.en: The noun update in British English puts the stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词 update 在英式英语中重音前移到第一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar page torn away: the word is about the difference between what is written and what is true now.
abstract.cn: 想象日历被撕下一页：这个词说的是「写着的」与「此刻为真的」之间的差距。

abstract.en: Nothing is updated once for ever; the word implies a clock that keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 没有东西能更新一次就永远有效：这个词暗含一只一直在走的钟。

abstract.en: The same word serves a file and a worried family, because both need the newest facts.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既用于文件也用于焦急的家人，因为两者都需要最新的事实。

examples.en: Please update your address in the school records.
examples.cn: 请在学校记录里更新你的地址。

examples.en: The manager updated us on the new schedule by email.
examples.cn: 经理通过邮件向我们通报了新日程。

examples.en: A small update will fix the problem with the printer.
examples.cn: 一次小的更新就能修好打印机的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普戴特」——阿普把日期戴特到最新一天：更新

root: 由英语副词 up（向上、达到）与 date（源自拉丁语 dare「给予」，经古法语 date「签发日期」入英语）合成，二十世纪出现，最初指使记录保持最新，计算机时代扩展为软件更新与新闻快报。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of update all close a gap between what is written and what is true now: a list, a family waiting for news, a program, a broadcast, or a whole building.
sensesIntro.cn: update 的五个义项都在弥合「写着的」与「此刻为真的」之间的差距：一份清单、等待消息的家人、一个程序、一则快报，或一整栋建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the calendar is turned to the newest day and the old page is torn off.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历被翻到最新的一天，旧页被撕下。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a list or file is brought to the present.
branches.cn: 记录线：清单或文件被带到当下。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: someone is told the latest facts.
branches.cn: 人群线：有人被告诉最新的事实。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a new version replaces the old one.
branches.cn: 程序线：新版本取代旧版本。

branches.en: THE NEWS: a short report on a moving story.
branches.cn: 新闻线：关于进行中事件的简短报道。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: lights and machines are made modern.
branches.cn: 建筑线：照明与设备被现代化。

intro.en: Update is two English words joined; only the second half carries a French and Latin history.
intro.cn: update 是两个英语词组合而成；只有后半部分带有法语与拉丁语的历史。

latinIntro.en: Dare is recorded Latin, and data is its plural participle; French date stands between them and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare 有记录，data 是其分词复数；法语 date 位于它们与英语之间。

definition_zh: 以免；免得；唯恐；生怕
definition_en: used to introduce a clause stating what must be prevented, and after verbs of fearing to mean that something may happen
core_image: 有人伸手按住正要合上的窗，怕风把桌上的纸吹散
scene: 傍晚起风了，妇人先把窗扇扣好，又把桌上的纸压在水杯下面，免得夜里一阵风把它们吹得满地。 Lest the wind scatter the letters, she weighted them under a cup.
sceneCN: 这里是「以免、免得」（第 1 个义项：引出要防止发生的事）；句意为免得风把信吹散，她用一只杯子压住了它们。图中可辨识物件：窗扇、桌上的纸页、压纸的水杯。

derivatives.zh: lest 由古英语 þy læs 缩合而来，læs 即今天的 less，故 less 是同源词而非严格派生词
由 un- 与 less 构成，义为「除非」，与 lest 同出表示「少一些条件」的词干
与 less 同属 little 的不规则三级阶梯，只是词义走向最高级，并非由 lest 派生

senses.title: So that something does not happen
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause naming an unwanted event that the action is meant to prevent
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出一个不想要的结果，说明前面的动作正是为了避免它
senses.example: Take an umbrella lest you get wet.
senses.exampleCN: 带把伞，免得淋湿。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning by the less, that is by a smaller chance, so the clause after it names the outcome one hopes to keep small.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原是一个意为「以更小的可能」的短语，因此它后面的从句说出的是希望被压到最小的那种结果。

senses.title: That something feared may happen
senses.definition: used after verbs such as fear or worry to introduce the thing one is afraid of
senses.definitionCN: 用于 fear、worry 等表示担心的动词之后，引出所怕之事
senses.example: She worried lest the letter should never arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心那封信永远到不了。
senses.why: If the clause no longer states a purpose but the content of a fear, the same small-chance phrase turns into a marker of anxiety rather than prevention.
senses.whyCN: 当从句不再说明目的，而是说出担心的内容时，同一个「可能很小」的短语就从「防止」转为「焦虑」的标志。

intro.en: Lest is a worn-down phrase rather than a root, and its history is the history of a comparison that turned into a conjunction.
intro.cn: lest 不是一个词根，而是一个磨薄了的短语；它的历史就是一个比较结构变成连词的历史。

items.en: The phrase þy læs þe meant by the less that, where læs is the ancestor of less and þe introduced the clause.
items.cn: 古英语短语 þy læs þe 意为「以更小的可能」，其中 læs 是 less 的先祖，þe 引出从句。

items.en: In this period the phrase was already written together in some texts, and it carried the sense of preventing an outcome.
items.cn: 在这一时期，一些文本已把它连写，并带有「防止某种结果」的意思。

items.en: Middle English reduced the phrase to leste and then lest, dropping the comparative word until only the conjunction remained.
items.cn: 中古英语把短语缩为 leste，再缩为 lest，比较级的词干被磨掉，只剩下连词。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used lest freely with should and with the bare subjunctive, as in lest he fall.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者随意地把 lest 与 should 或光秃的虚拟式连用，如 lest he fall。

items.en: Modern English keeps lest mainly in formal and literary prose, where it survives beside the plainer in case and so as not to.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lest 主要保留在正式与文学性文字里，与更朴素的 in case、so as not to 并存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words that share the small-chance phrase behind lest; the near-meaning group gathers the plainer ways of saying the same thing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 lest 背后那个「可能很小」的短语有关的词；近义组收表达同一意思的更朴素说法。

entries.definition: The comparative word hidden inside lest, meaning a smaller amount.
entries.definitionCN: 藏在 lest 里面的比较级词，表示更少的量。

entries.definition: If not, built from less, and close in spelling but different in grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「除非」，由 less 构成，拼写相近但语法作用不同。

entries.definition: The superlative of little, from the same smallness family.
entries.definitionCN: little 的最高级，与 lest 同属表示「小」的词族。

entries.definition: Final or most recent; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 最后的；最近的。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A plainer way to name a possible event one wants to be ready for.
entries.definitionCN: 更朴素的说法，引出需要提防的可能情况。

entries.definition: A plain negative purpose phrase used in everyday prose.
entries.definitionCN: 日常文字中表示否定目的的朴素说法。

entries.definition: The full form of the fear sense that lest compresses.
entries.definitionCN: lest 所压缩的「担心」义的完整说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a fossil of a comparison, so its memory hooks should all start from the little phrase it used to be.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个比较结构的化石，所以记忆钩子都该从它曾经是的那小短语出发。

normal.en: Lest comes from the phrase by the less, so the clause after it is the outcome you want to keep small.
normal.cn: lest 来自「以更小的可能」这一短语，所以它后面的从句就是你希望压小的结果。

normal.en: The less is still visible in the spelling, and that is also why unless belongs to the same family.
normal.cn: 拼写里还看得见 less，这也是 unless 属于同一家族的原因。

normal.en: Lest takes should or the bare subjunctive in older prose: lest he fall, lest it be thought.
normal.cn: 在较早的文字里，lest 后面用 should 或光秃的虚拟式：lest he fall、lest it be thought。

normal.en: In modern plain writing, in case and so as not to do the same job with fewer syllables.
normal.cn: 在现代平实文字里，in case 与 so as not to 用更少的音节做同样的事。

normal.en: Lest is rare enough that seeing it is a signal of formal or literary register, not of everyday speech.
normal.cn: lest 相当少见，见到它就说明语体正式或带文学性，而不是日常口语。

abstract.en: A phrase that once measured chance became a single word that guards a door.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经衡量可能性的短语，变成了一个守门的单词。

abstract.en: To say lest is to name the bad outcome first and the precaution second, which is worry given grammar.
abstract.cn: 说 lest 就是先点出坏结果、再给预防，这是把担心写成了语法。

abstract.en: Words wear down: a whole comparison survives as four letters and a warning.
abstract.cn: 词会被磨薄：一整套比较最后只剩四个字母和一句警告。

examples.cn: 带把伞，免得淋湿。

examples.cn: 她担心那封信永远到不了。

examples.en: He spoke softly, lest anyone hear.
examples.cn: 他轻声说话，生怕有人听见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来是」——小声点，免得「来是」麻烦；lest 是以免。

root: 古英语短语 þy læs þe（以更小的可能）缩合而成，其中 læs 即 less 的先祖；一般认为与 little、less、least 同源。

sensesIntro.en: There is one core job, keeping an unwanted outcome small, which splits into a purpose sense and a fear sense according to what the clause reports.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心工作只有一件：把不想要的结果压小；按从句所报告的内容，它分成「目的」与「担心」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a window shut before the wind can scatter the papers.
core.cn: 核心意象：风还没把纸吹散，一只手先把窗按住。

intro.cn: 这个词由一整套比较短语构成，因此这里的条目是那个短语的各部分，以及它磨薄之后的形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

intro.cn: billion 在法语中由 bi- 与 million 组合而成。

definition_zh: 复数；复数形式；复数的；不止一个的
definition_en: the grammatical form that refers to more than one person or thing; a word standing in that form; and, more widely, consisting of or involving more than one group or kind
core_image: 黑板上的词尾添了一笔，旁边画着两个并排的小人
scene: 老师在黑板上把单词的结尾改了一笔，又在旁边画了两个并排的小人。 The plural of child is children, not childs.
sceneCN: 这里 plural 是「复数」（第 1 个义项：表示不止一个的语法形式）；句意为 child 的复数形式是 children，而不是 childs。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、两个小人。

derivatives.zh: 由 plural 加 -ity 构成，义为「多数；复数性；相对多数票」
由 plural 加 -ize 构成，义为「使变成复数；使多样化」
由 pluralist 加 -ic 构成，义为「多元主义的；多元的」

senses.title: The grammatical form for more than one
senses.definition: the form of a word that refers to more than one person, thing or instance
senses.definitionCN: 指不止一个人、物或实例的词的形式
senses.example: The plural of child is children, not childs.
senses.exampleCN: child 的复数形式是 children，不是 childs。
senses.why: Latin pluralis meant belonging to more than one, and Roman grammarians used it for the number category opposed to singular; English borrowed the label and keeps it for the category itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pluralis 意为「属于不止一个的」，罗马语法学家用它指与单数相对的数范畴；英语借来这个标签，至今用它指这个范畴本身。

senses.title: A word standing in the plural form
senses.definition: a word or word form used when more than one is meant, such as books or children
senses.definitionCN: 表示不止一个时使用的词或词形，如 books 或 children
senses.example: Write the sentence again, this time with the verb in the plural.
senses.exampleCN: 把这句话重写一遍，这次动词用复数形式。
senses.why: Once the grammar category had a name, speakers could point at a single printed word and call it a plural, so the noun also names the form on the page rather than only the abstract category.
senses.whyCN: 语法范畴有了名称之后，人们就能指着纸上某一个词说它是复数，因此这个名词也用来指纸上的那个形式，而不只是抽象范畴。

senses.title: Consisting of more than one kind
senses.definition: involving or consisting of more than one group, kind or point of view, especially in social and political description
senses.definitionCN: 涉及或由不止一个群体、种类或观点组成，尤用于社会与政治描述
senses.example: The city has a plural culture shaped by many immigrant communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市拥有由众多移民社群塑造的多元文化。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the Latin sense of belonging to many: anything built from more than one element can be called plural, and modern sociology uses it for societies that hold several cultures at once.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了拉丁语「属于多数」的意思：凡由不止一个要素构成的都能叫 plural，现代社会学用它指同时容纳多种文化的社会。

intro.en: Plural comes from Latin plus, more, through the adjective pluralis, which grammarians used for the number that marks more than one; Old French passed it to English.
intro.cn: plural 来自拉丁语 plus（更多），经形容词 pluralis 而来，语法学家用它指标记「不止一个」的数；古法语把它传给英语。

items.en: Plus meant more, and its genitive pluris, of more, supplied the stem for words about number and quantity.
items.cn: plus 意为更多，其属格 pluris（更多的）为表示数量与多寡的词提供了词干。

items.en: Pluralis meant of or belonging to more than one, and Roman grammarians used it for the number category opposed to singularis.
items.cn: pluralis 意为「属于不止一个的」，罗马语法学家用它指与 singularis（单数）相对的数范畴。

items.en: Old French plurel carried the grammatical term into French, and English took the word from it.
items.cn: 古法语 plurel 把这个语法术语带进法语，英语又从法语借入。

items.en: Middle English plural named the grammatical number and, by extension, a word standing in that number.
items.cn: 中古英语 plural 指语法上的复数，又引申指处于该数形式的词。

items.en: Modern English adds the wider adjective use for anything made of several parts, and the derived family of plurality and pluralism.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上更宽的形容词用法，指任何由多个部分构成的东西，并派生 plurality 与 pluralism 一族词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words built on the Latin stem for more; the near-meaning group gathers the grammatical opposite and words for several things at once.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「更多」词干上的词；近义组收语法上的对立项与表示「多个」的词。

entries.definition: Existing in large numbers.

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin stem for more, and the family keeps counting: one, more than one, and the many groups that a society can hold.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「更多」的词干上，词族一直在数数：一个、不止一个，以及一个社会能容纳的许多群体。

normal.en: Latin plus means more, and pluralis means belonging to more than one, so the grammatical label and the everyday adjective share one stem.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 plus 意为更多，pluralis 意为属于不止一个，所以语法标签与日常形容词共用一个词干。

normal.en: The plural of most English nouns adds -s or -es, but a few keep older forms such as children and feet.
normal.cn: 多数英语名词的复数加 -s 或 -es，但少数保留了 children、feet 这类更古老的形式。

normal.en: Plurality adds -ity to plural and names the state of being many, or the largest share of votes below half.
normal.cn: plurality 在 plural 后加 -ity，指「多」的状态，或未过半但最多的票数。

normal.en: Pluralism adds -ism, turning the fact of many into a position that many should be protected.
normal.cn: pluralism 加 -ism，把「有很多」这个事实变成「多应当受到保护」的立场。

normal.en: The adjective plural is not compared in grammar books, but more plural appears when writers compare how mixed two societies are.
normal.cn: 语法书不给形容词 plural 作比较，但作家比较两个社会的混合程度时会写 more plural。

abstract.en: A plural is a small machine for turning one thing into a crowd.
abstract.cn: 复数是一台小机器，把一个东西变成一群。

abstract.en: Every language draws a line between one and more than one, and this word is the English name of that line.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都在「一个」与「不止一个」之间画一条线，这个词就是那条线的英语名字。

abstract.en: A plural society is a sentence with many subjects and no single verb that can carry them all.
abstract.cn: 一个多元社会就像一句有许多主语、却没有一个动词能统领全部的句子。

examples.en: The plural of child is children, not childs.
examples.cn: child 的复数形式是 children，不是 childs。

examples.en: Write the sentence again, this time with the verb in the plural.
examples.cn: 把这句话重写一遍，这次动词用复数形式。

examples.en: The city has a plural culture shaped by many immigrant communities.
examples.cn: 这座城市拥有由众多移民社群塑造的多元文化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉」——一个人拉不动，大家一起来拉，人一多就是复数；记住 plural 是复数。

root: 拉丁语 plus（更多）→ 属格 pluris → 形容词 pluralis（属于不止一个的）→ 古法语 plurel → 中古英语 plural；同一词根 plur- 也生出 plurality、pluralism，核心都是「多」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the idea of more than one; the senses run from the grammatical category, to the word form that carries it, to the wider adjective for anything made of several kinds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「不止一个」这个观念；义项从语法范畴，走到承载它的词形，再到更宽的形容词用法，指任何由多种成分构成的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a final letter added to a word, with two small figures drawn beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：词尾添上一笔，旁边画着两个并排的小人。

branches.en: two children standing for the word children
branches.cn: 两个小人代表 children 这个词

branches.en: a final letter added to the end of a noun
branches.cn: 名词末尾添上的一笔

branches.en: a sentence rewritten with a plural verb
branches.cn: 把动词改成复数后重写的句子

branches.en: several communities sharing one street
branches.cn: 几个社群共用一条街

branches.en: a council in which many voices must be heard
branches.cn: 必须听见许多声音的议会

intro.en: The word is a Latin comparative stem turned into a grammatical adjective, and English extends it with suffixes of state, action and doctrine.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语比较级词干变成的语法形容词，英语又用表示状态、动作与主张的后缀来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded behind this word: plus, more, its genitive pluris, the adjective pluralis, and the later noun pluralitas.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后有可考的拉丁形式：plus（更多）、其属格 pluris、形容词 pluralis，以及较晚的名词 pluralitas。

definition_zh: 自由地；免费地；大量地
definition_en: without limits, without payment, or in large amounts
core_image: 孩子在开阔的草地上张开双臂奔跑
scene: 孩子们在草地上自由地奔跑。 The children ran freely on the grass.
sceneCN: 这里 freely 是「自由地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们在草地上自由地奔跑。

derivatives.zh: 自由的；免费的
自由

senses.title: Without limits
senses.definition: in a way that is not held back
senses.definitionCN: 以不受阻碍的方式
senses.example: The children ran freely on the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在草地上自由地奔跑。
senses.why: This is the adverb form of the basic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本义项的副词形式。

senses.title: Without payment
senses.definition: in a way that costs nothing
senses.definitionCN: 以不花钱的方式
senses.example: The samples were given freely to visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 样品免费送给参观者。
senses.why: Free as no cost becomes an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 「免费」的 free 转为副词即此义。

senses.title: In large amounts
senses.definition: in a generous or plentiful way
senses.definitionCN: 以慷慨或充足的方式
senses.example: Tears flowed freely at the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式上泪水纵横。
senses.why: What is not restricted can pour out.
senses.whyCN: 不受限制的东西会大量涌出。

intro.en: Freely is the old adverb built on free.
intro.cn: freely 是由 free 构成的古老副词。

items.en: Freo meant not a slave.
items.cn: freo 意为非奴隶的。

items.en: The adverb suffix -lice formed freelice.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -lice 构成了 freelice。

items.en: The form became freliche.
items.cn: 词形演变为 freliche。

items.en: It settled as freely.
items.cn: 最终定型为 freely。

items.en: It also means at no cost and in plenty.
items.cn: 它也表示免费和大量。

note.en: Freely is compared with words that look similar and words for openness.
note.cn: 把 freely 与形近词以及表示坦率、开放的词作比较。

entries.definition: kind and pleasant
recently
in an honest way
without hiding anything
in a giving way
easily and willingly

normalIntro.en: Freely is how a free action is done.
normalIntro.cn: freely 描述自由行动的方式。

normal.en: The children ran freely on the grass.
normal.cn: 孩子们在草地上自由地奔跑。

normal.en: The samples were given freely to visitors.
normal.cn: 样品免费送给参观者。

normal.en: Tears flowed freely at the ceremony.
normal.cn: 仪式上泪水纵横。

normal.en: You may speak freely in this room.
normal.cn: 在这个房间里你可以畅所欲言。

normal.en: The river flows freely after the ice melts.
normal.cn: 冰融化后河水自由流淌。

abstract.en: A free step leaves no mark of a chain.
abstract.cn: 自由的脚步不会留下锁链的痕迹。

abstract.en: What is given freely cannot be taken for granted.
abstract.cn: 免费给予的东西不应被视为理所当然。

abstract.en: Freely means the door is already open.
abstract.cn: freely 意味着门已经敞开。

examples.en: The children ran freely on the grass.
examples.cn: 孩子们在草地上自由地奔跑。

examples.en: You may speak freely in this room.
examples.cn: 在这个房间里你可以畅所欲言。

examples.en: The samples were given freely to visitors.
examples.cn: 样品免费送给参观者。

dict_mnemonic.text: free（自由的；免费的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= freely；同一个副词既能表示「不受限制」，也能表示「不收费」。

root: 由古英语 frēo（非奴隶的）加副词后缀 -līce 构成，核心义「以自由的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Freely means without limits, without payment, or in large amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: freely 意为自由地、免费地或大量地。

core.en: An action done with nothing in the way.
core.cn: 毫无阻碍地完成动作。

branches.en: Children run across the open grass.
branches.cn: 孩子们跑过开阔的草地。

branches.en: A gift is placed in a visitor hand.
branches.cn: 礼物被放到参观者手中。

branches.en: Tears come without being stopped.
branches.cn: 泪水不受阻挡地涌出。

branches.en: An open road and an open hand share one adverb.
branches.cn: 开阔的道路与张开的手共用一个副词。

branches.en: What is given without limit can also come in plenty.
branches.cn: 不受限制地给予，也就会大量到来。

intro.en: Freely shows free plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: freely 展示了 free 加副词后缀 -ly 的构成。

latinIntro.en: Freely is Germanic and is not built from Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: freely 属日耳曼语，不由拉丁词根构成。

items.example: The door lets air move freely.
items.exampleCN: 这扇门让空气自由流通。

items.example: Water flows freely in the stream.

definition_zh: 跨度；一段时间；涵盖
definition_en: the distance across something, a period of time, or to cover a length of time
core_image: 一座拱桥横跨两岸，桥身连成一个完整的弧
scene: 这座桥的跨度很大。 The bridge has a wide span.
sceneCN: 这里 span 是「跨度」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥的跨度很大。

derivatives.zh: 翼展
寿命
扳手；跨度物

senses.title: The distance across
senses.definition: the distance from one side of something to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从某物一侧到另一侧的距离
senses.example: The bridge has a wide span.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的跨度很大。
senses.why: This is the physical sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的物理含义。

senses.title: A period of time
senses.definition: a length of time between two points
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间的一段时间
senses.example: He lived in the city for a short span.
senses.exampleCN: 他在那座城市住了一段时间。
senses.why: Time is measured with the same image as distance.
senses.whyCN: 时间用与距离相同的意象来丈量。

senses.title: To cover a length
senses.definition: to last through or extend across a period or distance
senses.definitionCN: 持续经过或横跨一段时间或距离
senses.example: Her career spanned forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业生涯跨越了四十年。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for covering a span.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示覆盖一段跨度的动词。

intro.en: Span once meant the distance between an outstretched thumb and little finger.
intro.cn: span 最初指张开拇指与小指之间的距离。

items.en: Spann meant the width of a stretched hand.
items.cn: spann 意为张开手所量的宽度。

items.en: The form became span and named a measure.
items.cn: 词形变为 span，指一种量度。

items.en: It named the distance across a bridge or arch.
items.cn: 它指桥或拱的跨越距离。

items.en: It extended to periods of time.
items.cn: 它扩展到时间段。

items.en: The verb came to mean to cover or last through.
items.cn: 动词开始表示横跨或持续。

note.en: Span is compared with look-alike words and words for extent.
note.cn: 把 span 与形近词以及表示范围、长度的词作比较。

entries.definition: to turn quickly
to look over quickly
to produce eggs
the distance from side to side
the length of time something lasts
a continuous length

normalIntro.en: A span is a hand's reach used to measure the world.
normalIntro.cn: span 是用一手的伸展去丈量世界。

normal.en: The bridge has a wide span.
normal.cn: 这座桥的跨度很大。

normal.en: He lived in the city for a short span.
normal.cn: 他在那座城市住了一段时间。

normal.en: Her career spanned forty years.
normal.cn: 她的职业生涯跨越了四十年。

normal.en: The eagle has a huge wingspan.
normal.cn: 这只鹰的翼展很大。

normal.en: Children have a short attention span.
normal.cn: 孩子的注意力持续时间很短。

abstract.en: A span is a bridge between two ends.
abstract.cn: 跨度，是两端之间的一座桥。

abstract.en: A life is a span measured by what fills it.
abstract.cn: 一生是一段跨度，由填满它的东西丈量。

abstract.en: The hand that measures also connects.
abstract.cn: 用来丈量的手，也在连接。

examples.en: The bridge has a wide span.
examples.cn: 这座桥的跨度很大。

examples.en: He lived in the city for a short span.
examples.cn: 他在那座城市住了一段时间。

examples.en: Her career spanned forty years.
examples.cn: 她的职业生涯跨越了四十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: span 是跨度、一段时间；life span 是「寿命」，attention span 是「注意力持续时间」，wingspan 是「翼展」；过去式和过去分词都是 spanned。

root: 来自古英语 spann（张开手量的宽度），核心义由手的跨度扩展为桥的跨距、时间的跨度与跨越动作。

sensesIntro.en: Span means a distance across, a period of time, or to cover a length.
sensesIntro.cn: span 指横跨的距离、一段时间，或跨越一段长度。

core.en: The reach between two outstretched points.
core.cn: 两个伸展点之间的触及范围。

branches.en: An arch joins two banks.
branches.cn: 一道拱连接两岸。

branches.en: A calendar page turns from year to year.
branches.cn: 日历一页页翻过一年又一年。

branches.en: A career runs from youth to old age.
branches.cn: 一段职业从青年延续到老年。

branches.en: Distance and time are both measured by reach.
branches.cn: 距离与时间，都用「触及」来丈量。

branches.en: To span time is to hold both ends at once.
branches.cn: 跨越时间，就是同时握住两端。

intro.en: Span forms a verb paradigm and several compound nouns.
intro.cn: span 构成动词变化形式和若干复合名词。

latinIntro.en: Span has no Latin root; it comes from Old English spann.
latinIntro.cn: span 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 spann。

items.example: The bridge has a wide span.

items.exampleCN: 她的职业生涯跨越了四十年。

items.example: A bridge spanning the river was built.
items.exampleCN: 一座横跨河流的桥建成了。

items.meaning: the width of a bird's wings
items.example: The eagle has a huge wingspan.

definition_zh: 创新的；革新的；有创意的
definition_en: introducing or using new ideas, methods, or designs
core_image: 一双手把旧图纸翻过来，背面画着完全不一样的方案
scene: 实验室的桌面上摊着旧方案和新草图。 Her innovative approach to packing cut shipping costs by half.
sceneCN: 这里 innovative 是「有创意的、创新的」（第 1 个义项：引人新想法或新方法），句意为她创新的包装办法把运费降了一半。画面里能看到的物件：旧图纸、新草图、计算器。

pos.zh: 形容词：创新的；有创意的

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「创新；新事物」
同族动词，义为「革新；创新」
由词干加 -or 构成，义为「创新者」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「有创意地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「创新性」

senses.title: Introducing new ideas
senses.definition: using or introducing new ideas and original methods rather than copying old ones
senses.definitionCN: 使用或引入新想法、独创新方法，而不是照搬旧办法
senses.example: The school hired an innovative teacher who turns grammar into games.
senses.exampleCN: 学校请了一位把语法变成游戏的创新老师。
senses.why: The verb innovate plus the adjective ending -ive gives "having the quality of bringing in the new".
senses.whyCN: 动词 innovate 加上形容词词尾 -ive，得到「具有引入新事物之性质的」。

senses.title: Original and well designed
senses.definition: designed in a clever and original way, often praised for its design
senses.definitionCN: 以巧妙、独创的方式设计，常因设计受到称赞
senses.example: The lamp has an innovative folded-paper shade.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯有一个构思新颖的折纸灯罩。
senses.why: The same quality moves from methods to objects: a thing can be called innovative when its design itself is the new idea.
senses.whyCN: 同一性质从方法移到物件：当设计本身就是新想法时，这个物件也叫 innovative。

senses.title: Ahead of the market
senses.definition: working in a way that is unusually advanced for the industry at the time
senses.definitionCN: 以在当时的行业里格外先进的方式运作
senses.example: Investors look for small innovative firms before they grow famous.
senses.exampleCN: 投资人会在小公司出名之前寻找那些领先创新的小企业。
senses.why: Business writing stretched the adjective to describe companies and markets that act before their rivals do.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个形容词扩用到先于对手行动的公司与市场上。

intro.en: Innovative is the noun innovation reshaped with the Latin adjective ending -ivus, which came down as English -ive.
intro.cn: innovative 是在名词 innovation 之上换用拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus（英语作 -ive）而成。

items.en: Novus "new" is the root that also gives novel and renovate.
items.cn: novus「新的」是词根，也给出 novel、renovate。

items.en: Innovare "to make new inside, renew" supplied the verb stem.
items.cn: innovare「使里面变新、更新」提供了动词词干。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning "tending to do".
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示「倾向于做……」的形容词。

items.en: Innovative appears in English in the eighteenth century, first in writing about politics and trade.
items.cn: innovative 在十八世纪英语中出现，最初见于讨论政治与贸易的文字。

items.en: Twentieth-century advertising turned it into a standard word of praise for products.
items.cn: 二十世纪的广告把它变成了赞美产品的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the nov- stem; the near-meaning group holds other adjectives of newness and originality.
note.cn: 形近组共享 nov- 词干；近义组收其他表示「新」与「独创」的形容词。

entries.definition: Full of original ideas; built on the Latin root for "make", not on novus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有创造力的」，词根是拉丁语「制造」，与 novus 无关。

entries.definition: New and unusual, from the same Latin novus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新颖的」，来自同一拉丁词 novus。

entries.definition: To renew an old building with the prefix re-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翻新」，前缀 re- 表「再次」。

entries.definition: Good at thinking up new things, said of people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「善于发明的」，多形容人。

entries.definition: Different from anything else, not following others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独创的」，强调与任何东西都不同。

entries.definition: A compound describing a person who thinks inventively.
entries.definitionCN: 复合形容词，形容善于创新思考的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the -ive ending to a quality you can see in a person or a design.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 -ive 词尾与能从人身上或设计中看到的性质联系起来。

normal.en: innovation is the thing, innovative is the quality that produced it.
normal.cn: innovation 是产物，innovative 是产生它的那种性质。

normal.en: The -ive ending marks an adjective of tendency, as in active and creative.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 表示倾向性的形容词，如 active、creative。

normal.en: An innovative approach often costs less than the old one.
normal.cn: 创新的办法往往比旧办法更省钱。

normal.en: Investors chase innovative firms before they are famous.
normal.cn: 投资人会在公司出名前追逐创新企业。

normal.en: Use more innovative instead of innovativer; the word takes more.
normal.cn: 比较级要用 more innovative，不能写 innovativer。

abstract.en: Think of flipping an old drawing over to find a new plan on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象把一张旧图纸翻过来，背面画着新方案。

abstract.en: Innovative is a door that opens outward, away from habit.
abstract.cn: innovative 像一扇朝外开的门，远离习惯。

abstract.en: A truly innovative idea looks strange before it looks obvious.
abstract.cn: 真正创新的想法先显得奇怪，后来才显得理所当然。

examples.en: They praised her innovative use of cheap materials.
examples.cn: 他们称赞她创新地使用了廉价材料。

examples.en: An innovative design does not always sell well.
examples.cn: 创新的设计并不总是卖得好。

examples.en: The clinic is known for its innovative treatments.
examples.cn: 这家诊所因其创新疗法而闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一脑维新」——脑子里总做维新，人就显得有创意

root: 由拉丁语 novus「新的」→ novare「使变新」→ innovare「更新」构成的词干，加上形容词词尾 -ivus（英语 -ive）。因此 innovative 字面是「带有更新倾向的」，与 innovation、innovate、innovator 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: new in method, new in design, and advanced for the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：方法上新、设计上新，以及在市场中格外先进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old drawing is flipped over and a completely different plan shows on the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧图纸被翻过来，背面是完全不同的方案。

branches.en: THE METHOD: teaching, packing or working in a new way.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：用新方式教学、包装或工作。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a clever design can carry the adjective itself.
branches.cn: 物件这条线：巧妙的设计本身就能承载这个形容词。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a company acts before its rivals and is called innovative.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：公司先于对手行动，被称为创新。

branches.en: THE LINK: whether person, method or object, the quality is the same.
branches.cn: 连接线：不论是人、方法还是物件，性质是同一个。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word is almost always praise in advertising.
branches.cn: 语气线：在广告里这个词几乎总是褒义。

intro.en: Innovative is innovat- plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus, English -ive.
intro.cn: innovative 由 innovat- 加拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus（英语 -ive）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms novus, novare and innovare are attested; the suffix -ivus is a regular adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus、novare、innovare 都有记载，-ivus 是规则的形容词词尾。

items.example: The prefix marks the movement into a new state.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标出向内进入新状态的动作。

items.example: The same root appears in novel.
The verb stem carries the action.
It turns the action into a quality.
The noun names the thing produced.
A close adjective from a different root.
items.exampleCN: 另一个词根的近义形容词。

items.example: The most general word of the group.

latinEntries.meaning: tending to, having the quality of

definition_zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角
definition_en: a curved piece of glass or plastic that bends light, the matching part of the eye, the glass element of a camera, and a way of looking at a subject
core_image: 一枚弧形玻璃片把远处的灯光收成一个小亮点
scene: 摄影师的桌上，一枚弧形玻璃片被布擦得发亮，远处的灯在它里面缩成一点。 He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜头」（第 3 个义项：相机上那片可更换的玻璃）；句意是他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。图中可辨识物件：擦镜布、弧形玻璃片、桌上的相机。

pos.zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角

derivatives.zh: 由 lens 与 man 复合而成，义为「摄影师；镜头工作者」
由 lens 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无镜片的」
源自拉丁语小词 lenticula，义为「透镜状的；小扁豆形的」

senses.title: A curved piece of glass that bends light
senses.definition: a shaped piece of glass or plastic used to focus or spread light in an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 仪器中用来聚光或散光的成形玻璃片或塑料片
senses.example: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。
senses.why: The word starts as the name of a lentil, because a biconvex piece of glass has the same plump oval shape as the seed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只是「小扁豆」的名字，因为双凸的玻璃片和那颗种子一样呈饱满的椭圆。

senses.title: The light-focusing part of the eye
senses.definition: the small clear structure inside the eye that focuses images on the retina
senses.definitionCN: 眼球内把影像聚焦到视网膜上的透明小结构
senses.example: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。
senses.why: Once lens names any shaped body that focuses light, the eye's own focusing body takes the same name by analogy of function.
senses.whyCN: 既然 lens 能指任何聚光的成形体，眼睛自带的聚光结构就按功能类比得到了同一个名字。

senses.title: The glass element of a camera
senses.definition: the glass unit fitted to a camera, often one of several that can be exchanged
senses.definitionCN: 装在相机上的玻璃组件，常为可更换的若干支之一
senses.example: He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。
senses.why: A camera is built around the same bending of light that a single lens performs, and the whole glass assembly simply borrows the part's name.
senses.whyCN: 相机正是围绕单片镜片所做的同一件弯光之事造出来的，于是整组玻璃组件干脆沿用了零件的名字。

senses.title: A way of looking at a subject
senses.definition: a particular standpoint that shapes how a subject is understood
senses.definitionCN: 决定人们如何理解某个主题的特定立场
senses.example: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
senses.exampleCN: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。
senses.why: A lens decides what enters the eye and how it is bent, so the word naturally becomes a metaphor for whatever selects and shapes our view.
senses.whyCN: 镜片决定什么进入眼睛、又如何被弯曲，于是这个词很自然地成了比喻，指那些筛选并塑造视野的东西。

intro.en: Lens is Latin for lentil; the optical sense was borrowed by seventeenth-century writers because a biconvex glass looked like the seed.
intro.cn: lens 在拉丁语里就是「小扁豆」；十七世纪的学者借它来指光学镜片，因为双凸玻璃的形状像那颗种子。

items.en: Lens, with the stem lent-, named the lentil, the small flat seed of a plant in the pea family.
items.cn: lens（词干 lent-）指小扁豆，即豆科植物那种小而扁的种子。

items.en: The diminutive lenticula named a small lentil and later supplied English lentil and the adjective lenticular.
items.cn: 小词形式 lenticula 指一颗小扁豆，后来为英语提供了 lentil 与形容词 lenticular。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers of optics borrowed lens for a curved piece of glass, since a biconvex shape resembles a lentil.
items.cn: 十七世纪的光学作者借 lens 指弧形玻璃片，因为双凸形状与扁豆相似。

items.en: English took lens as a technical term of microscopy and astronomy, where curved glass was newly powerful.
items.cn: 英语把 lens 当作显微镜与天文学的技术术语引入，那时弧形玻璃刚刚显示出威力。

items.en: Modern English extended lens to the eye's own focusing body, to camera optics and to any selective point of view.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lens 扩展到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机光学，以及任何有筛选作用的视角。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the seed word behind the name and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group collects other optical parts that bend or split light.
note.cn: 形近组收这个名字背后的「种子」词及其派生形式；近义组收其他弯曲或分解光线的光学部件。

entries.definition: The small flat seed that gave the lens its name.
entries.definitionCN: 给透镜命名的这种小而扁的种子。

entries.definition: Shaped like a lentil or a lens.
A photographer or cameraman, especially in news work.
Made or working without a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 无镜片的；不用镜片工作的。

entries.definition: The hard transparent material that lenses are usually made from.
entries.definitionCN: 制作镜片常用的坚硬透明材料。

entries.definition: A shaped piece of glass that splits light into colours.
entries.definitionCN: 把光分解成多种颜色的成形玻璃。

entries.definition: A lens or device that makes small things look bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 使小东西看起来更大的镜片或装置。

entries.definition: The lens or lens group you look through in an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器上供眼睛观看的那片或那组镜片。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for a seed, and the whole optical family keeps returning to that plump oval shape and to the bending of light.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里是一颗种子，整个光学词族反复回到那个饱满的椭圆形状与弯折的光线。

normal.en: Latin lens means lentil, so the glass was named for its shape rather than for its function.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lens 意为扁豆，所以这片玻璃是因形状得名，而不是因功能得名。

normal.en: Lentil and lens share one root: the seed and the glass are the same oval seen at different sizes.
normal.cn: lentil 与 lens 同根：种子与玻璃是同一个椭圆在不同尺度上的样子。

normal.en: Lenticular adds -ar to the Latin diminutive and means shaped like a lentil or a lens.
normal.cn: lenticular 在拉丁小词后加 -ar，意为「扁豆状或透镜状的」。

normal.en: Lensless adds -less: an instrument without that curved piece cannot focus anything.
normal.cn: lensless 加 -less：少了那片弧形玻璃，仪器就什么也聚不了。

normal.en: Through the lens of is the phrase to keep: it turns an optical part into a way of judging.
normal.cn: 要记住 through the lens of 这个说法：它把一片光学零件变成了一种评判方式。

abstract.en: A seed, a glass, an eye and a standpoint all answer to one word, because each of them selects and focuses what comes through.
abstract.cn: 种子、玻璃、眼睛与立场都由同一个词承担，因为它们都在筛选并聚焦穿过自己之物。

abstract.en: The history of lens shows how a name for shape can quietly become a name for power: the power to decide what is seen.
abstract.cn: lens 的历史说明，一个形状之名可以悄悄变成能力之名：决定什么能被看见的能力。

abstract.en: Calling a view a lens reminds us that no standpoint is perfectly clear glass; every one bends what it shows.
abstract.cn: 把视角称作 lens，提醒人没有任何立场是毫无偏折的玻璃，每一种都会弯折它所呈现的东西。

examples.en: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
examples.cn: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。

examples.en: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
examples.cn: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。

examples.en: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「棱子」——镜片边缘像棱子；记住 lens 是透镜、镜片。

root: 拉丁语 lens（小扁豆，词干 lent-）→ 十七世纪借作光学名词，因双凸镜片形似扁豆 → 现代英语扩展至晶状体、相机镜头与看待事物的视角。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a lentil-shaped glass that bends light; the senses then move to the eye's own focusing body, the camera's glass unit, and the metaphor of a selective standpoint.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是形似扁豆、弯折光线的玻璃；义项由此转到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机的玻璃组件，以及「有筛选作用的立场」这一比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small curved glass disc on a cloth, gathering a distant lamp into one bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：布上一枚小小的弧形玻璃片，把远处的灯收成一个亮点。

branches.en: a glass disc bending a beam onto a slide
branches.cn: 把光束弯到载玻片上的玻璃片

branches.en: a pupil widening in a dim room
branches.cn: 暗房里慢慢张开的瞳孔

branches.en: a photographer wiping the front glass
branches.cn: 摄影师擦拭最前那片玻璃

branches.en: a historian reframing an old quarrel
branches.cn: 重新框定旧日争吵的历史学家

branches.en: a documentary filmed from one angle
branches.cn: 只从一个角度拍摄的纪录片

intro.en: The word is a Latin seed name, its diminutive and a Latin suffix, and English then builds the optical compounds and negatives that surround it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「种子」名、它的小词形式与一个拉丁后缀构成，英语再围绕它造出光学复合词与否定义。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a cover for a camera lens

definition_zh: 漏；漏出；漏洞；泄露（秘密）
definition_en: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole; to give out secret information; a hole through which something escapes, or the information disclosed
core_image: 水管接缝处慢慢渗出的一滴水珠
scene: 厨房水管接头处渗出水来，地上很快积了一小片。 A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
sceneCN: 这里是「漏出」（第 1 个义项：液体从孔洞中漏出）；句意是管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。图中可辨识物件：水管接头、水珠、地面的水迹。

derivatives.zh: 由 leak 加 -age 构成，义为「泄漏；泄漏量」
由 leak 加 -y 构成，义为「漏的；爱泄露的」
由 leak 加 -er 构成，义为「泄密者」

senses.title: To let liquid or gas escape
senses.definition: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole or crack
senses.definitionCN: 让液体或气体从孔洞、裂缝中跑出来
senses.example: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。
senses.why: The Middle English verb named a slow dripping escape, so the physical movement of liquid is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语的动词指缓慢滴漏地跑掉，所以液体实际的移动是最早的义项。

senses.title: A hole through which something escapes
senses.definition: a hole or crack through which liquid or gas escapes
senses.definitionCN: 液体或气体借以跑出的孔洞或裂缝
senses.example: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。
senses.why: If a thing leaks, the opening that allows the escape can take the same name, turning the action into the place where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 某物会漏，那么允许它跑出的开口也能用同一个名字，于是动作变成了动作发生的位置。

senses.title: To give out secret information
senses.definition: to give secret information to someone who should not have it
senses.definitionCN: 把秘密信息交给不该得到它的人
senses.example: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。
senses.why: Information escapes like liquid: once the barrier is broken, what was contained spreads beyond its intended boundary.
senses.whyCN: 信息像液体一样跑掉：一旦屏障破了，原本被盛住的东西就会扩散到不该去的地方。

senses.title: The secret information disclosed
senses.definition: the secret information that has been disclosed
senses.definitionCN: 被泄露出去的秘密信息
senses.example: The leak forced the minister to explain himself in public.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露的消息迫使部长公开作出解释。
senses.why: By the same shift as the hole, the noun can name the disclosed material rather than the act of disclosing it.
senses.whyCN: 和「漏洞」一样的转喻，名词可以指被泄露的内容，而不是泄露这个动作。

intro.en: Leak is a Germanic word of uncertain exact origin, probably related to Dutch and Norse verbs for dripping; English extended it from water to secrets.
intro.cn: leak 是日耳曼语词，确切来源不确定，很可能与荷兰语、古诺斯语中表示滴落的动词有关；英语把它从水扩展到秘密。

items.en: A Germanic source is generally assumed, but the exact reconstructed form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为源自日耳曼语，但确切的重构形式并不确定。

items.en: Middle Dutch leken meant to drip or to let liquid through.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 leken 意为滴下或让液体透过。

items.en: Old Norse leka carried a similar sense of running or dripping.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 leka 有相近的「流淌、滴落」之意。

items.en: Middle English leken named the slow escape of liquid from a container.
items.cn: 中古英语 leken 指液体从容器中慢慢漏出。

items.en: Modern English extended the verb to secrets, and made the noun mean both the hole and the disclosure.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到秘密，并让名词同时指漏洞与泄露的内容。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives and one homophone; the near-meaning group collects verbs of liquid and secrets escaping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词和一个同音词；近义组收表示液体或秘密跑掉的动词。

entries.definition: The act of leaking, or the amount that escapes.
Letting liquid through; not watertight.
A person who gives secret information to others.
A long green vegetable related to the onion; it sounds the same but has a different history.
entries.definitionCN: 一种与洋葱近亲的长绿蔬菜；它与 leak 同音，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall in small drops, usually slowly.
To let liquid flow out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 意外让液体从容器中流出。

entries.definition: To get out of a place where something is held.
entries.definitionCN: 从被盛放或困住的地方跑出来。

entries.definition: To make secret information known.

normalIntro.en: The word starts with liquid finding a way out; its suffixes build the amount, the quality and the person, and one homophone is a vegetable.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从液体找到出口开始；它的后缀造出量、性质和人物，而一个同音词是蔬菜。

normal.en: Leak began with liquid escaping through a small opening, which is why every later sense keeps the idea of a breach.
normal.cn: leak 起初指液体从小口跑出，所以后来每个义项都保留「破口」的想法。

normal.en: Leakage adds -age and names the process or the amount, not the hole itself.
normal.cn: leakage 加 -age，指过程或数量，而不是孔洞本身。

normal.en: Leaky adds -y and turns the verb into an adjective: a leaky bucket is one that lets water through.
normal.cn: leaky 加 -y，把动词变成形容词：leaky bucket 就是会漏水的水桶。

normal.en: Leaker adds -er and names the person who lets information out.
normal.cn: leaker 加 -er，指把信息放出去的人。

normal.en: Leek is only a homophone: the vegetable's name has a different origin and nothing to do with dripping.
normal.cn: leek 只是同音词：这种蔬菜的名字来源不同，与滴漏无关。

abstract.en: Containers fail at their edges, and so do institutions, which is why a word for a hole serves for a secret.
abstract.cn: 容器常在边缘失效，机构也是如此，所以一个表示孔洞的词能用来指秘密。

abstract.en: What leaks is always something that was meant to stay inside, so the word carries a quiet accusation.
abstract.cn: 漏出的东西总是本该留在里面的东西，所以这个词带着一种安静的指责。

abstract.en: A single drop is enough to prove the barrier has failed, which is why leaks are found before they are measured.
abstract.cn: 一滴就足以证明屏障已经失效，所以人们总是先发现漏点，再去测量漏量。

examples.en: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
examples.cn: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。

examples.en: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
examples.cn: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。

examples.en: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
examples.cn: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哩可」——水从缝里「哩可」一下跑出来；leak 是漏。

root: 日耳曼语来源，一般认为与中古荷兰语 leken、古诺斯语 leka（滴落、渗漏）有关；确切词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is liquid finding a way out; the senses divide into the opening, the disclosure of secrets and the disclosed material itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是液体找到出口；义项由此分为孔洞、秘密的泄露，以及被泄露的内容本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop forming at a pipe joint and falling to the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：水管接缝处凝成一滴水珠，落到地面。

branches.en: water finding a crack in an old pipe
branches.cn: 水在旧管子上找到一道裂缝

branches.en: a plumber's torch aimed behind a sink
branches.cn: 水管工的手电照向水槽后面

branches.en: a document passed to a journalist in secret
branches.cn: 一份文件被秘密交给记者

branches.en: a headline built from information that escaped
branches.cn: 用跑出来的信息做成的头条

branches.en: a wet floor under a joint that will not seal
branches.cn: 封不住的接头下方湿了一片地面

intro.en: A Germanic verb gains three English suffixes for amount, quality and person, while a homophone vegetable stays unrelated.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语动词加三个英语后缀，分别表示数量、性质和人物；同音的蔬菜词则并无关系。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

the act or amount of leaking

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有某种性质

definition_zh: 有争议的；引起争论的；未有定论的
definition_en: causing strong public disagreement, or still open to doubt
core_image: 一个话题被两群人从两边同时拉住
scene: 新规定一贴出，楼下立刻分成两拨人争论。 The new rule proved highly controversial.
sceneCN: 这里 controversial 指「有争议的」（第 1 个义项：让众人激烈争论的）；句意是新规定被证明极具争议。

pos.zh: 有争议的；引起争论的；未有定论的

senses.title: Causing strong argument
senses.definition: making people argue strongly about it
senses.definitionCN: 让众人为此激烈争论的
senses.example: The plan is controversial among farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案在农民中很有争议。
senses.why: A question with two loud answers will not sit still.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题若有两个响亮的答案，就安静不下来。

senses.title: Debated in public
senses.definition: publicly questioned by many people over time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间被许多人在公共场合质疑的
senses.example: His record remains controversial today.
senses.exampleCN: 他的履历至今仍引起争论。
senses.why: A public story can be told two ways for a long time.
senses.whyCN: 一个公开的故事，能被两种讲法讲很久。

senses.title: Not settled
senses.definition: still open to doubt because no side has won
senses.definitionCN: 因为没有任何一方胜出而仍可怀疑
senses.example: Whether the drug helps is still controversial.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药是否有效仍无定论。
senses.why: Evidence that points both ways keeps a verdict waiting.
senses.whyCN: 两向都指的证词，让判决迟迟不来。

intro.en: Controversial comes from Latin controversia, a dispute, from controversus, turned in the opposite direction, built on contra-, against, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: controversial 来自拉丁语 controversia（争执），源于 controversus（转向反面），由 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn or turn around.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动或转身。

items.en: Controversus meant turned against or facing the other way.
items.cn: controversus 意为转过来相对或朝着反面。

items.en: Controversia named a dispute between turned sides.
items.cn: controversia 指两方相对而起的争执。

items.en: French controverse kept the sense of a public quarrel.
items.cn: 法语 controverse 保留了公开争吵之义。

items.en: English controversy was used for religious debate.
items.cn: 英语 controversy 曾用于宗教辩论。

items.en: The adjective now covers any widely disputed matter.
items.cn: 形容词如今涵盖任何广受争议的事情。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other words for what is argued over.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示被争辩之事的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a question that splits a crowd, then move to a long public story and a verdict that never comes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从把人群分成两半的问题开始，再到讲得很久的公开故事，最后到迟迟不来的判决。

normal.en: Controversial is the adjective of controversy: it makes a quarrel.
normal.cn: controversial 是 controversy 的形容词：它制造争吵。

normal.en: Contra- is against and vers is turn, so the word is about sides turning against each other.
normal.cn: contra- 是相对，vers 是转，这个词讲的是两方转过身来对着彼此。

normal.en: A controversial rule is one that no one can quietly obey.
normal.cn: 有争议的规定，是没人能安静照做的那种规定。

normal.en: A figure can stay controversial for a hundred years.
normal.cn: 一个人物可以争议上百年。

normal.en: Two loud answers, no settled question.
normal.cn: 两个响亮的答案，一个没有定下来的问题。

abstract.en: Picture two crowds pulling one rope from both ends.
abstract.cn: 想象两群人在绳子两端对拉。

abstract.en: Picture a headline that divides a breakfast table.
abstract.cn: 想象一条把早餐桌分成两半的新闻标题。

abstract.en: Picture a scale stuck level, with neither side down.
abstract.cn: 想象一架卡在水平位置的天平，两边都不落下。

examples.en: The choice of site was highly controversial.
examples.cn: 选址极具争议。

examples.en: He wrote a controversial book about the war.
examples.cn: 他写了一本关于这场战争的有争议的书。

examples.en: The method remains controversial among doctors.
examples.cn: 这种方法在医生中仍有争议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 controversial 记成 contro（相对）加 vers（转）加 ial：两方转过身来对着彼此争，就是有争议的。

root: 源自拉丁语 controversus（转向反面），由 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成，经 controversia（争执）加 -al 成为形容词。

sensesIntro.en: From a question that splits a crowd, to a long public story, and at last to a verdict that has not arrived.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把人分成两半的问题，到讲得很久的公开故事，最后到还没有到来的判决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two crowds pulling one rope from opposite ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：两群人在绳子两端对拉。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the power to cause argument.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是引起争吵的力量。

branches.en: The second sense keeps the argument in public view.
branches.cn: 第二个义项让争论一直待在公众视野里。

branches.en: The third sense says the question is still open.
branches.cn: 第三个义项说这个问题仍然敞着。

branches.en: Argument that lasts becomes public controversy.
branches.cn: 持续下去的争吵会变成公开争议。

branches.en: Where the public keeps arguing, no verdict settles.
branches.cn: 公众一直争的地方，判决也定不下来。

intro.en: Controversial is built on Latin contra-, against, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: controversial 由拉丁语 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vers- also appears in convert, divert and reverse.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vers- 也出现在 convert、divert 与 reverse 中。

core_image: 一包被引线点燃、即将炸开的火药
scene: 警方拆除了一枚爆炸装置。 Police defused an explosive device.
sceneCN: 这里 explosive 是「会爆炸的、易爆的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警方拆除了一枚爆炸装置。

senses.title: Able to explode
senses.definition: able or likely to explode
senses.definitionCN: 能够爆炸或容易爆炸的
senses.example: The workers found an explosive device near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在桥附近发现了一枚爆炸装置。
senses.why: The core sense is the power to burst apart.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是具有炸裂的力量。

senses.title: Likely to erupt
senses.definition: likely to cause a sudden violent reaction or very fast growth
senses.definitionCN: 很可能引发突然的激烈反应或极快增长的
senses.example: The region saw explosive growth in tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的旅游业出现了爆炸式增长。
senses.why: Physical bursting becomes sudden social change.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的炸开转为社会的骤然变化。

senses.title: An explosive substance
senses.definition: a substance that can explode
senses.definitionCN: 能够爆炸的物质
senses.example: The mine stores explosives in a secure shed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场把炸药存放在安全的棚屋里。
senses.why: The quality becomes a physical material.
senses.whyCN: 性质变成一种具体的物质。

intro.en: Explosive comes from Latin explodere, to drive off by clapping, through explosion.
intro.cn: explosive 经 explosion 来自拉丁语 explodere，原意为「用拍手声赶走」。

items.en: Ex- means out and plaudere means to clap.
items.cn: ex- 意为向外，plaudere 意为拍手。

items.en: Explodere means to drive an actor off by clapping.
items.cn: explodere 意为用拍手声把演员赶下台。

items.en: Explosion becomes the word for a violent burst.
items.cn: explosion 成为表示猛烈爆裂的名词。

items.en: Explosive describes what can burst.
items.cn: explosive 描述能够爆裂的事物。

items.en: Explosive also describes fast growth and tense situations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 explosive 也可形容快速增长与紧张局势。

note.en: Explosive means able to burst; expensive means costing a lot.
note.cn: explosive 是会爆炸的，expensive 则是昂贵的。

entries.definition: costing a lot of money
limited to a small group
showing feelings clearly
easily changing or exploding
likely to change or break suddenly
able to catch fire and burn

normalIntro.en: Explosive describes materials that burst and situations that may erupt.
normalIntro.cn: explosive 既形容会爆裂的物质，也形容可能爆发的局势。

normal.en: The bomb squad carried the explosive away.
normal.cn: 拆弹小组把爆炸物运走了。

normal.en: The market showed explosive growth last year.
normal.cn: 去年市场出现了爆炸式增长。

normal.en: The debate turned explosive within minutes.
normal.cn: 辩论几分钟内就变得火药味十足。

normal.en: Hydrogen is highly explosive in the wrong conditions.
normal.cn: 在不当条件下，氢气极易爆炸。

normal.en: The report warned of an explosive situation.
normal.cn: 报告警告说局势一触即发。

abstract.en: Picture a spark touching a trail of powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗火星碰到火药引线。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd that suddenly erupts in anger.
abstract.cn: 想象人群突然爆发出愤怒。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line shooting straight up.
abstract.cn: 想象一条几乎垂直上升的曲线。

examples.en: The army cleared the field of explosives.
examples.cn: 军队清除了战场上的爆炸物。

examples.en: Explosive population growth put pressure on housing.
examples.cn: 爆炸式的人口增长给住房带来压力。

examples.en: The chemical is too explosive to store indoors.
examples.cn: 这种化学品太易爆，不能存放在室内。

dict_mnemonic.text: explode（爆炸）加形容词后缀 -ive，就是「会爆炸的」，即 explosive。

root: 源自拉丁语 explodere（用拍手声赶下台），经 explosion（爆裂）形成形容词 explosive，核心义「会爆开的」。

sensesIntro.en: Explosive means able to explode, likely to cause a sudden eruption, or a substance that explodes.
sensesIntro.cn: explosive 意为会爆炸的、可能突然爆发的，或炸药。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark reaching a trail of powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：火星触到火药引线。

branches.en: The base sense is the ability to burst.
branches.cn: 基础义是具有爆裂的能力。

branches.en: Bursting becomes sudden growth or anger.
branches.cn: 爆裂转为骤然增长或愤怒。

branches.en: The quality becomes a physical material.
branches.cn: 性质变成具体的物质。

branches.en: A device and a situation can both be explosive.
branches.cn: 装置与局势都可能是爆炸性的。

branches.en: Explosive growth and stored explosives share the idea of force.
branches.cn: 爆炸式增长与储存的炸药都带有力量之意。

intro.en: Explosive belongs to the explode family, built on Latin ex- out and plaudere to clap.
intro.cn: explosive 属于 explode 词族，由拉丁语 ex-（向外）与 plaudere（拍手）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin explodere and explosio are the source forms of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 explodere 与 explosio 是该词族的来源形式。

items.example: The box held an explosive charge.
The old shell could still explode.

这种气体可能爆炸性燃烧。

items.exampleCN: 爆炸的炮弹照亮了天空。

definition_zh: 开端；开始；起点；启程
definition_en: the beginning of an event or period, the starting point from which a process develops, or, in an older sense, the act of setting out on a journey
core_image: 清早的木门被推开，一个人背着行囊跨出门槛，小路一直伸向远处
scene: 集会刚开始时，长桌旁的人都没有开口，主持人看了看表，把手中的纸摊平。 At the outset of the meeting, nobody wanted to speak first.
sceneCN: 这里的 outset 是「开端、开始」（第 2 个义项：一场活动或一段时期的开头）；句意为会议刚开始时没人愿意先开口。图中可辨识物件：长桌、手表、摊平的纸。

collocations.phrase: at the outset of the war

derivatives.zh: 与 outset 同由 set 复合而成，前缀换成 on（压上来），义为「开始；发作」
与 outset 同由 set 复合而成，介词换成 off（离开），义为「抵消；补偿」
outset 所自出的短语动词，义为「出发；着手做」

senses.title: The act of setting out on a journey
senses.definition: the act of starting a journey or setting off, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 动身开始一段行程的行为，是这个词最老的义项
senses.example: The travellers made an early outset before the roads grew busy.
senses.exampleCN: 旅人们在道路变拥挤之前早早启程。
senses.why: Outset began as the noun of the phrase set out, which meant to leave on a journey, so the oldest sense still carries the picture of feet crossing a doorway.
senses.whyCN: outset 起初是短语 set out（出发、启程）的名词形式，所以最老的义项仍带着「双脚跨出门槛」的画面。

senses.title: The beginning of an event or period
senses.definition: the point in time at which an event, a meeting or a period begins
senses.definitionCN: 一件事、一场会议或一段时期开始的那一刻
senses.example: At the outset of the meeting, nobody wanted to speak first.
senses.exampleCN: 会议刚开始时，没人愿意先开口。
senses.why: Once the noun named the moment of leaving, it could name the opening moment of anything at all, and that is how a word about journeys became a word about meetings and wars.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词本指「离开」的那一刻，它就能指任何事情的开头一刻，于是关于行程的词变成了关于会议与战争的词。

senses.title: The starting point a process grows from
senses.definition: the first stage of a process, plan or career, seen as what everything later grows out of
senses.definitionCN: 过程、计划或事业的第一个阶段，后来的东西都由它长出来
senses.example: The design was too costly from the outset.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计从一开始就太昂贵。
senses.why: If the word marks the first moment of an event, it can also mark the point a process starts from, which is why from the outset means from the very first stage and not merely at some early time.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出一件事的最初一瞬，它也能标出一个过程起步的那一点，所以 from the outset 指从最初阶段起，而不只是某个较早的时候。

intro.en: Outset is a noun made from the phrasal verb set out, to start a journey; it appeared in English in the sixteenth century and now lives almost only inside the fixed phrases at the outset and from the outset.
intro.cn: outset 是由短语动词 set out（出发）转成的名词，十六世纪出现在英语中，如今几乎只活在 at the outset 与 from the outset 这两个固定说法里。

items.en: Settan meant to set, to place or to cause to sit, and it is the source of the modern verb set.
items.cn: settan 意为放置、使坐下，是现代动词 set 的来源。

items.en: Ūt meant out, and with a verb of movement it marked the point of leaving a place.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外，与表示移动的动词连用时标出离开某处的那一点。

items.en: The phrase set out meant to begin a journey or an undertaking, and it was common in travel and in accounts of work.
items.cn: 短语 set out 意为启程或着手一项事务，在旅行记述与工作记录中很常见。

items.en: The noun outset was formed from that phrase and first meant a setting out, a departure.
items.cn: 名词 outset 由这个短语转成，最初指「出发、启程」。

items.en: The sense widened from a departure to the beginning of anything, and the word is now rare outside a few fixed phrases.
items.cn: 词义从「启程」扩展到任何事情的开头，如今除了少数固定说法以外已很少单独使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built on set; the near-meaning group collects nouns for a first point in time.
note.cn: 形近组收由 set 构成的复合词；近义组收表示时间上「最初一点」的名词。

entries.definition: The beginning of something unpleasant, such as an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 不愉快之事（如疾病）的开始；发作。

entries.definition: Something that balances or cancels another effect.
The time when the sun goes down and the sky reddens.
entries.definitionCN: 太阳落下、天色转红的时刻。

entries.definition: To make someone unhappy, worried or slightly ill.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人不快、担忧或有点不舒服。

entries.definition: The first part or the first moment of something.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的第一部分或最初一刻。

entries.definition: The point at which an activity begins.
A formal word for a beginning, also used for a graduation ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 「开始」的正式说法，也指毕业典礼。

entries.definition: The point from which something develops or is derived.
entries.definitionCN: 事物由之发展或得来之处。

normalIntro.en: Outset is a phrase turned into a noun, so its hooks keep the motion of stepping out of a door rather than any abstract idea of time.
normalIntro.cn: outset 是一句短语变成的名词，所以记忆钩子保留的是迈出门的那一步，而不是抽象的时间概念。

normal.en: The word is out plus set, and the pair simply reverses the phrase set out, to start a journey.
normal.cn: 这个词是 out 加 set，只是把短语 set out（出发）的次序调了过来。

normal.en: Nearly every modern use sits inside a fixed phrase, at the outset or from the outset, and the word rarely stands alone.
normal.cn: 现代用法几乎都嵌在 at the outset 或 from the outset 这样的固定说法里，这个词很少单独出现。

normal.en: Onset is the darker twin: an onset is usually something you dread, while an outset is simply a start.
normal.cn: onset 是它偏暗的孪生词：onset 通常是令人惧怕之事的发作，而 outset 只是平白的开头。

normal.en: Offset keeps set but turns the start into a counterweight, so the two compounds pull in opposite directions.
normal.cn: offset 也留着 set，却把「开始」变成了砝码，于是这两个复合词方向相反。

normal.en: Outset is formal and a little literary; a spoken sentence usually prefers start or beginning.
normal.cn: outset 偏正式、略带孩子气的文气；口语里通常更愿意用 start 或 beginning。

abstract.en: A word that began with stepping out of a door still reminds us that every beginning is also a move away from somewhere.
abstract.cn: 一个从迈出门槛起步的词提醒人：每一个开始同时也是离开某处的动作。

abstract.en: To say a plan was wrong from the outset is to claim the error was already there before the first step was taken.
abstract.cn: 说一个方案从一开始就错了，就是主张错误在迈出第一步之前已经存在。

abstract.en: Naming a start fixes a point in time, and after that point every account of events has somewhere to stand.
abstract.cn: 给开始命名，就是在时间里钉下一个点，此后每一种叙述都有了立足之处。

examples.en: At the outset of the meeting, nobody wanted to speak first.
examples.cn: 会议刚开始时，没人愿意先开口。

examples.en: The design was too costly from the outset.
examples.cn: 这个设计从一开始就太昂贵。

examples.en: The travellers made an early outset before the roads grew busy.
examples.cn: 旅人们在道路变拥挤之前早早启程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特塞特」——奥特把行囊塞好就出门，出门就是开头；记住 outset 是开端、启程。

root: 由古英语 ūt（向外）与 settan（放置）构成，最初是短语 set out（出发）的名词形式，义为「启程」，后泛指一切开端；set 属日耳曼语词，无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a step out of a doorway; the senses divide into the departure itself, the opening moment of an event, and the first stage a process grows from.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是迈出门槛的那一步；义项按「启程本身」「一件事的开头一刻」「过程由之起步的最初阶段」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden door pushed open at dawn, a traveller with a pack stepping over the sill, the path running far ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：清早的木门被推开，一个人背着行囊跨出门槛，小路一直伸向远处。

branches.en: a traveller leaving before the road fills
branches.cn: 趁路上人少就动身的旅人

branches.en: a long table where nobody speaks yet
branches.cn: 还没人开口的一张长桌

branches.en: a plan already too expensive on paper
branches.cn: 在纸上就已经太贵的方案

branches.en: a meeting and a plan both have a first stage
branches.cn: 会议与方案都有各自的最初阶段

branches.en: the same noun for leaving and for beginning
branches.cn: 同一个名词，既指动身，也指开端

intro.en: The word joins a direction adverb to a verb of placing, and the result names the moment something is set to go outward.
intro.cn: 这个词把方向副词与表示放置的动词结合，命名的是「某物被摆出去」的那一刻。

latinIntro.en: Outset is built from Old English settan and ūt, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound.
latinIntro.cn: outset 由古英语 settan 与 ūt 构成，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to put or to fix in place

examples.cn: 他对那晚的叙述里有矛盾。

examples.en: The two rules stand in direct contradiction.
examples.cn: 这两条规则直接相抵触。

examples.en: Her calm contradiction silenced the meeting.
examples.cn: 她平静的反驳让会场安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contradiction 记成 contra（反对）加 dict（说）：两句话互相反着说、彼此顶住，就是矛盾。

root: 源自拉丁语 contradicere（反着说），由 contra-（反对）与 dicere（说）构成，指两说相冲、反驳与自相矛盾。

sensesIntro.en: From two claims that cannot both stand, to a voice raised against one, and at last to a phrase that cancels itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不能同时成立的两句话，到对其中一句发出的反对，最后到自我抵消的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows leaving one bow in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭从同一张弓上朝相反方向飞出。

branches.en: Two statements cannot both be true at once.
branches.cn: 两句话不能同时为真。

branches.en: A person may also speak against a claim.
branches.cn: 人也可以出声反对某种说法。

branches.en: A phrase can fight inside itself.
branches.cn: 一个短语能在自身内部打起架来。

branches.en: A clash of claims and a voice against it are neighbours.
branches.cn: 说法的冲突与反对的声音是邻居。

branches.en: To deny and to self-cancel both undo a statement.
branches.cn: 否认与自我抵消，都是在拆掉一句话。

intro.en: Contradiction is built on contra-, against, plus dicere, to say.
intro.cn: contradiction 由 contra-（反对）与 dicere（说）构成。

latinIntro.en: The saying base dict- also appears in dictionary, dictate and verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 说话词基 dict- 也出现在 dictionary、dictate 与 verdict 中。

items.meaningCN: 一种说法顶着另一种说法

items.meaning: to say the opposite of a claim
items.meaningCN: 说出与某说法相反的话

items.meaning: the way words are chosen and spoken

items.example: Look the word up in a dictionary.

items.meaning: to say words for another to write
a formal decision spoken in court
